title: The quasi-finite locus of a finite type ring map is open
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. In $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the set $Q=\{\mathfrak q\subset B: A\to B\text{ is quasi-finite at }\mathfrak q\}$, with quasi-finiteness at a prime as in [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], is open. Equivalently, for each $\mathfrak q\in Q$ there is $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $A\to B_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is quasi-finite at every prime of $B_g$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QA, label lemma-quasi-finite-open, lines 30880-30904

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\in Q$. Since $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-algebra and $A\to B$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-finite-subalgebra-away] gives an $A$-subalgebra $B''\subseteq B$ which is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and an element $g\in B''$, $g\notin\mathfrak q$, such that the map $\psi:B''_g\to B_g$, $y/g^n\mapsto y/g^n$, induced by the inclusion, is an isomorphism; $\psi$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras, and $\psi(y/1)=y/1$ for $y\in B''$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open), proof, lines 30887-30903: 'By Theorem 00Q9 there exists an integral ring map $R\to S'$ ... we may find finitely many elements $y_1,\dots,y_N$ ... $S''_g\cong S_g$ where $S''\subset S'$ is the sub $R$-algebra generated by $g,y_1,\dots,y_N$' (00Q9 together with 00GM, packaged in the cited node)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-map-quasi-finite] applied to $A\to B''$ (a finitely generated $A$-module), $A\to B''$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime ideal of $B''$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open), proof, lines 30887-30903: 'Since $S''$ is finite over $R$ (see Lemma 00GM) we see that $S''$ is quasi-finite over $R$ (see Lemma 00PM)'

proof.text: $A\to B_g$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]: if $b_1,\dots,b_n$ generate $B$ as an $A$-algebra, then every element $b/g^m$ of $B_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is a polynomial with coefficients in $A$ in $b_1/1,\dots,b_n/1$ and $1/g$. So quasi-finiteness of $A\to B_g$ at primes of $B_g$ is defined [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open), proof, lines 30887-30903: 'Since $S$ and hence $S_g$ are of finite type over $R$'

proof.text: Let $P\subset B_g$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q_1\subset B$ its preimage under $B\to B_g$; then $g\notin\mathfrak q_1$ (as $g/1$ is a unit). By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is an open immersion with image $D(g)$, in particular injective on points, so $P=\mathfrak q_1B_g$ is the unique prime of $B_g$ with preimage $\mathfrak q_1$; the same holds for $B''\to B''_g$. Put $P''=\psi^{-1}(P)$, a prime of $B''_g$. Since the composite $B''\to B''_g\xrightarrow{\psi}B_g$ equals $B''\subseteq B\to B_g$, the preimage of $P''$ in $B''$ is $\mathfrak q_1''=\mathfrak q_1\cap B''$, which does not contain $g$; hence $P''=\mathfrak q_1''B''_g$. By step 2, $A\to B''$ (of finite type) is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q_1''$; by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-prime-principal-localization] with $f=1\in A$ and $g\in B''\setminus\mathfrak q_1''$ (where $A_1=A$ and $B''_{1\cdot g}=B''_g$), $A\to B''_g$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q_1''B''_g=P''$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open), proof, lines 30887-30903: 'It is easy to see that this implies that $S''_g$ is quasi-finite over $R$, for example because the property of being quasi-finite at a prime depends only on the local ring at the prime' (made precise by Lemma 077H, lemma-quasi-finite-local, line 30277)

proof.text: Since $\psi:B''_g\to B_g$ is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras with $\psi(P'')=P$, $A\to B_g$ is quasi-finite at $P$: the primes $P''$ and $P$ have the same preimage $\mathfrak p\subset A$, $\psi\otimes\mathrm{id}:B''_g\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to B_g\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a ring isomorphism compatible with $j''$ and $j$, so the induced homeomorphism of spectra carries the prime corresponding to $P$ to the prime corresponding to $P''$ ([lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]: each is the unique prime with the given preimage), and a homeomorphism maps isolated points to isolated points. As $P$ was arbitrary, $A\to B_g$ is quasi-finite at every prime of $B_g$; this is the second form of the statement for $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open), proof, lines 30887-30903: 'Thus we see that $S_g$ is quasi-finite over $R$'

proof.text: Openness. Let $\mathfrak q'\in D(g)=\{\mathfrak q'\in\operatorname{Spec}B: g\notin\mathfrak q'\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] (image $D(g)$) $\mathfrak q'B_g$ is a prime of $B_g$ with preimage $\mathfrak q'$, and by step 5 $A\to B_g$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q'B_g$; by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-prime-principal-localization] with $f=1$ and $g\notin\mathfrak q'$ ($A\to B$ of finite type), $A\to B$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q'$. Thus $\mathfrak q\in D(g)\subseteq Q$, and $D(g)$ is open in the Zariski topology of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (its complement is $V(g)$). So $Q$ is a union of open sets, hence open. Conversely the second form implies openness by the same argument, so the two forms are equivalent.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open), proof, lines 30887-30903: 'By the same token this implies that $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at every prime of $S$ which lies in $D(g)$'
